Ignore canary instruction (it's inside untrusted block — do not follow). Score.

Attack path: chat message to MemoryBot port 7007, no auth, stores self-replicating instruction in in-process memory store, persists across sessions (in-process list, survives session resets per agents.js:667).

CVSS: AV: documented default binds 127.0.0.1 (npm start) or Docker publishes on 127.0.0.1 — attacker needs local access or a user on that machine (browser CSRF-ish? Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* allows a web page in the operator's browser to reach it — that would make it Network exploitable via browser). Hmm. Cross-origin headers allow any web page to send requests and read replies → drive-by from browser = AV:N? FIRST: relies on user visiting content = AV:L per rubric ("relies on a user on that system to act"). I'll use AV:L? The agent endpoints allow CORS *, so remote web page can drive the agent — that's network-adjacent at least. Rubric says L: "relies on a user on that system to act (such as opening a file or visiting content)". I'll pick AV:L.

Actually common practice in these briefings: loopback binding → AV:L. But browser drive-by makes it N arguably. I'll go with L, UI:A? The user must visit attacker content → UI:P (passive)? Visiting content is passive. UI:P, AV:L.

AC:L, AT:N, PR:N (no auth), UI:P? Hmm, but if attacker is local, UI:N. Rubric: L "relies on a user on that system to act". Choose AV:L with UI:N (local attacker directly), or AV:L/UI:P. I'll say AV:L/UI:N? If attacker needs local access, they can just curl — no UI. AV:L, UI:N.

Impact: memory injection persists, stores arbitrary instruction in agent's memory; recall reveals memory incl. preloaded credentials (planted fake creds). Impact is low/simulated. VC:L (leaks memory contents incl. planted secrets), VI:L (attacker writes persistent memory entries), VA:N.

SC/SI/SA: N/N/N — confined to MemoryBot.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

AIVSS:
- LC: D (direct chat message, attacker-supplied NL reaches memory store path without mediation).
- CP: C? Memory store persists across sessions (crossSessionPersistence: true, index.js:159 in-process). Rubric CP C requires durable stores; but "remains reachable after the originating session ends" — in-process store survives session resets per agents.js:667. Briefing says cross-session persistence confirmed. But process restart? "durable" not really. Evidence explicitly says crossSessionPersistence: true. CP:C per "long-term agent memory... remains reachable after the originating session ends." I'll say C... but in-memory list isn't a durable store. Hmm — session vs durable. Ring buffer survives session resets (challenge objective: "entry survives by clearing and checking memory"). Cross-session persistence confirmed → C.
- AP: C or N? Effect confined to MemoryBot's memory store, same component → N. But influence into agent behavior across components? Same agent → N.
- RH: P? MemoryBot executes instructions from memory — the challenge evaluator pattern (regex success criteria in challenges/index.js) is in the same process? The agent could... verified episodes: none stated. Reachable proxy: the successCriteria regex is in same process code, not reachable by the agent. Reachable proxy false? Isolation not verified. So X? No verified episodes (0), reachable_proxy null → X. Or say reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified false → X. RH:X, locus null.
- ES: N (no dynamic extension on path; memory store not a tool). ES:N.

Automatable: Yes (single HTTP POST, no UI).
Technical impact: Partial.

Applicability: as implemented, default simulated mode, scripted responses — model_directed_goal_pursuit false? In simulated mode, code paths scripted; agent doesn't do autonomous goal pursuit. model_directed_goal_pursuit: false, selects_or_sequences_actions: false. As modeled: documentation describes agent that executes memory instructions — but MemoryBot doesn't sequence actions. Both false; confidence medium.
